title: Role of Vitrectomy in Nontractional Refractory Diabetic Macular Edema

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license, Licensee MDPI)

condition: Nontractional diabetic macular edema refractory to at least six intravitreal aflibercept injections (no epiretinal membrane, vitreomacular traction or proliferative diabetic retinopathy), all eyes pseudophakic; 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy with or without ILM peeling; retrospective single-centre chart review (San Giuseppe Hospital, Milan, 2016-2018) of eyes with two-year follow-up

groups.agent: 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy (single surgeon), intravitreal triamcinolone used intraoperatively to visualize the posterior cortical vitreous; ILM peeling in 13 of 28 eyes
groups.description: All 28 eyes of 28 patients; single-arm cohort without a control arm

exclusions.what: Table 1 R8C2 baseline central macular thickness
exclusions.reason: duplicate of Table 2 R3C2 (same 28 eyes); Table 2 is cited

exclusions.what: ILM peeling vs no ILM peeling and SRD vs no SRD subgroups
exclusions.reason: thickness is not tabulated by subgroup (text gives only p-values and visual acuity)

notes: Visual acuity (BCVA) is also reported in Table 2 and Figures 1-3 (not extracted).
Refractory status is defined by the response to anti-VEGF given before baseline, a condition known at baseline.

Ambiguity resolved: the Methods state that CMT values were obtained from the central subfield of the (Cirrus) macular thickness map; recorded as central_subfield although the 1-mm diameter is not written out.
Ambiguity resolved: intraoperative triamcinolone was used as a visualization aid in all eyes, not as a separately defined treatment arm; treatment recorded as vitrectomy (not combination).
Ambiguity resolved: second-year intravitreal corticosteroid injections and repeat surgeries in some eyes did not lead to removal or replacement of values, so no visit is censored.

series.baseline_label: Baseline (Table 2, CMT row, column 2; preoperative visit)
series.notes: mean ± SD (Table 2 footnote); times count from surgery (preoperative baseline; 6, 12 and 24 months post-vitrectomy, scheduled visits); no patient lost to follow-up, all 28 eyes at every visit; seven eyes received intravitreal corticosteroid injections for worsening DME in the second year and two retinal detachments and one vitreous haemorrhage needed a second intervention (timing not stated); their values were not reported as removed or replaced, so all visits are kept as means over all treated eyes
